title: Pointers
description: Learn about pointers, memory addresses, and how to work with reference types in Go
theory:
## Pointers in Go

Pointers store memory addresses instead of values directly.

### Pointer Basics

```go
var p *int       // p is a pointer to int (nil initially)
x := 10
p = &x          // & gets address of x

fmt.Println(*p)  // * dereferences - prints 10
```

### Why Use Pointers?

1. **Modify the caller's variable** - pass by reference
2. **Avoid copying large data** - pass pointer to struct
3. **Create mutable data structures**

### The & Operator

& gets the memory address of a variable:
```go
x := 42
ptr := &x // ptr holds address of x
```

### The * Operator

* has two meanings:
- In a type declaration: `*int` means "pointer to int"
- In code: `*ptr` dereferences the pointer

```go
ptr := &x
value := *ptr // read value through pointer
*ptr = 99    // modify value through pointer
```

### The new Function

`new(Type)` allocates memory and returns a pointer:
```go
ptr := new(int)
*ptr = 42
```

### Pointers to Structs

```go
type Person struct {
    Name string
    Age  int
}

p := &Person{Name: "Alice", Age: 30}
p.Age = 31 // Can access fields directly on pointer
```

exercises.title: Declare a Pointer
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to an int named 'ptr' that points to a variable 'x' with value 42. Print the pointer value using fmt.Println(ptr).
hints: Use var ptr *int to declare a pointer to int
Use ptr = &x to assign the address of x to ptr
exercises.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    x := 42
    var ptr *int
    ptr = &x
    fmt.Println(ptr)
}

exercises.title: Dereference a Pointer
exercises.description: Create a pointer to an int and use the * operator to access and print the value it points to.
hints: Use ptr := &value to create a pointer
Use *ptr to dereference and get the value
exercises.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    value := 100
    ptr := &value
    fmt.Println(*ptr)
}

exercises.title: Pass Pointer to Function
exercises.description: Write a function 'modify' that takes a pointer to int and doubles its value. Call it with a variable and print the result.
hints: Inside modify, use *p = *p * 2 to double the value
Call modify(&num) to pass the address

exercises.title: Use the new Keyword
exercises.description: Use the 'new' keyword to allocate a new int pointer, assign a value to it, and print the dereferenced value.
hints: Use new(int) to allocate a new pointer
exercises.solution:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    ptr := new(int)
    *ptr = 99
    fmt.Println(*ptr)
}

exercises.title: Pointer to Struct
exercises.description: Define a Person struct with Name (string). Create a pointer to Person using & and set Name to "Bob". Print Name through the pointer.
hints: Use p.Name to access field through pointer

exercises.title: Nil Pointer Check
exercises.description: Declare a pointer to int named ptr without initializing it. Check if it is nil and print "nil" or the dereferenced value.
hints: Use var ptr *int to declare a nil pointer
Use if ptr == nil to check

exercises.title: Swap with Pointers
exercises.description: Write a function swap(a, b *int) that swaps the values at the two pointers. Call with x:=5, y:=10 and print after swapping.
